title: BIDS Specification Version 1.11.2-dev
retrieval_text: The BIDS specification is at version 1.11.2-dev. Released versions include: ...

ai_enrichment.description: BIDS specification version 1.11.2-dev represents the current development state of the Brain Imaging Data Structure standard. The `-dev` suffix indicates that this version corresponds to the main development branch on GitHub rather than a formally published stable release. It incorporates ongoing updates, clarifications, and new features that have not yet been finalized for public distribution.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: Users should understand that 1.11.2-dev is an unstable, pre-release version of the specification. While it reflects the latest community consensus and upcoming changes, it may contain breaking modifications, incomplete documentation, or features that are still subject to revision. Stable releases (e.g., 1.11.1, 1.11.0) are preferred for production datasets and formal publications.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Using a development version can lead to inconsistencies between dataset organization and validation tools. BIDS validators and schema-based tools often lag behind the specification's main branch, meaning files organized according to 1.11.2-dev rules might trigger false errors or warnings. Additionally, downstream tools and pipelines may not yet support new entities or metadata fields introduced in the development branch.
example_scenarios: A researcher prepares a dataset using the latest GitHub main branch to test a new behavioral data entity, but the official BIDS Validator flags it as invalid because the validator's schema has not been updated to match 1.11.2-dev.

A dataset's BIDS_VERSION file lists 1.11.2-dev, indicating it was curated using development rules. When shared with collaborators using stable-release tools, certain metadata clarifications from recent releases cause validation warnings.
A user checks the schema version (2.0.0-dev) alongside the specification version to ensure their custom validation scripts are aligned with the latest development changes before an official release.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Not applicable for version records. When working with development versions, verify that your validation tools and schema packages are updated to match the specification branch. For stable, reproducible datasets, consider aligning with the latest officially released version (e.g., 1.11.1) and updating the BIDS_VERSION file accordingly.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS specification follows semantic versioning, with development versions tracked on the main branch of the bids-standard/bids-specification repository. Stable releases are published as GitHub releases, accompanied by PDF documentation and updated schema packages. The associated schema version 2.0.0-dev indicates that the underlying JSON schema structure is also in a pre-release state.

title: Schema Version 2.0.0-dev
retrieval_text: The BIDS schema (machine-readable YAML definitions) is at version 2.0.0-dev.

ai_enrichment.description: The BIDS schema is a machine-readable representation of the BIDS standard, written in a custom YAML format. It defines the rules for filenames, entities, suffixes, and metadata fields. A schema version of 2.0.0-dev indicates that the dataset is being validated against a development version of the schema, which corresponds to an unreleased or experimental version of the BIDS specification (in this case, BIDS 1.11.2-dev).
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When a BIDS dataset reports a schema version of 2.0.0-dev, it means the validator or tool is using a development build of the schema definitions. This schema is actively being updated and may contain experimental features, new rules, or changes that are not yet part of a stable BIDS release. Users should be aware that validation results from this schema might differ from those produced by the stable schema, and some rules may change before the next official release.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Using a development schema can help users prepare for upcoming BIDS changes, test new features (like those in BIDS Extension Proposals), or debug issues related to schema updates. However, it may also produce warnings or errors for valid BIDS 1.x datasets if the development schema enforces stricter or modified rules. It is important to verify whether the development schema is intended for the current workflow.
example_scenarios: A researcher runs the BIDS Validator on a dataset and sees a warning about a new metadata field requirement introduced in the 2.0.0-dev schema, which was not required in the stable BIDS 1.9 schema.
A developer testing a new BIDS extension (e.g., Microscopy, BEP031) uses the 2.0.0-dev schema to ensure their dataset structure aligns with upcoming specification changes.
A user encounters a validation error regarding filename entity rules that are being updated in the development schema to allow additional characters like - or +.
common_causes: The BIDS Validator or bidsschematools is configured to use the dev branch or a development release.
The dataset's SCHEMA_VERSION file explicitly specifies 2.0.0-dev.
A tool automatically fetches the latest development schema for testing or preview purposes.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: If the development schema is not intended, check the configuration of your BIDS Validator or tool to ensure it is pointing to the stable schema version. Review the BIDS specification changelog to understand what changes are included in the 2.0.0-dev schema and determine if they affect your dataset. If you are intentionally testing against the development schema, ensure your dataset complies with the new rules or note that warnings/errors may be expected until a stable release is available.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS schema is maintained in the bids-standard/bids-specification repository and can be accessed as YAML files or a single dereferenced JSON file. The dev suffix indicates an ongoing development cycle, and features or rules may be added, modified, or removed before a stable release. The BIDS Validator also hosts separate stable and development instances to support this workflow.

title: Context Namespace: schema
summary: The 'schema' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'schema' context namespace provides access to schema information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The `schema` context namespace provides direct access to the BIDS schema definition during dataset validation. It is one of several namespaces automatically populated by the BIDS Validator to support rule evaluation.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: For BIDS Manager users, this means the validation engine can dynamically reference the official schema structure when checking files. Rather than relying on static, hardcoded rules, the validator uses this namespace to query schema definitions, ensuring that validation logic adapts automatically to the specific BIDS schema version being used.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: This namespace is fundamental to how the BIDS Validator maintains consistency across different BIDS versions. It allows validation rules to be schema-driven, meaning new modalities, entities, or metadata fields can be validated without rewriting core validation logic. Understanding this helps users recognize that validation behavior is tightly coupled to the schema version specified in their dataset.
example_scenarios: A validation rule checks whether a specific metadata key is officially recognized in the current schema before validating its format.

When processing a new imaging modality, the validator uses the `schema` namespace to load the corresponding file type definition and automatically applies the correct naming conventions and metadata requirements.
During cross-file validation, rules reference the `schema` namespace to verify that associated files match the expected structure defined in the schema.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This is an internal validator context provided automatically by the BIDS Validator. No user action or configuration change is required.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `schema` namespace operates alongside other context namespaces such as `dataset`, `subject`, `sidecar`, `entities`, and `json`. It is part of the machine-readable BIDS schema system, which serves as the single source of truth for rendering the specification and driving validation.

title: Context Namespace: dataset
summary: The 'dataset' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'dataset' context namespace provides access to dataset information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'dataset' context namespace is a read-only object within the BIDS Validator that represents the aggregated state and properties of the entire dataset being validated. It is constructed once from the dataset's file tree and remains constant throughout the validation process, unlike file-specific or subject-specific contexts which are built dynamically for each file.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: For BIDS Manager users, the 'dataset' namespace is an internal validator construct that provides a stable reference to the whole dataset during rule evaluation. It is not a file entity or metadata field, but a structural reference used by the validator to enforce rules that depend on dataset-wide consistency, such as verifying required top-level files or comparing properties across subjects and sessions.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Understanding the 'dataset' context helps users interpret validation messages that reference dataset-level checks. Many BIDS rules rely on this constant context to ensure cross-file consistency, validate dataset_description.json, or enforce inheritance principles across the entire study structure.
example_scenarios: A validation rule checks that all subjects in a dataset have at least one functional run by referencing the constant dataset context to aggregate subject-level information.
The validator uses the dataset context to verify that dataset_description.json exists and contains required fields before proceeding with per-file checks.
Cross-modal validation rules compare metadata across different data types (e.g., ensuring T1w and T2w images share the same acquisition parameters) using the stable dataset reference.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This is an internal validator construct and does not require direct user modification. If validation errors reference dataset-level properties, users should verify that top-level dataset files (like dataset_description.json) are correctly formatted and that the directory structure matches BIDS expectations.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The dataset context is built once via buildDatasetContext(fileTree) and is passed to both per-file and dataset-level validation checks. While the dataset object remains constant, the validator dynamically builds subject, entities, sidecar, and association contexts for each file it inspects.

title: Context Namespace: subject
summary: The 'subject' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'subject' context namespace provides access to subject information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The `subject` context namespace is a component of the BIDS validation context that aggregates properties and contents related to the current subject directory being inspected. It is constructed once per subject directory and remains available while the validator processes all files within that subject's scope. According to the BIDS schema, it contains subject-level information, such as the collection of sessions present for that subject.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager or the BIDS Validator inspects a dataset, it builds a dynamic context for each file. For files located inside a subject folder (e.g., `sub-01/`), the `subject` namespace is populated with data relevant to that specific subject. This allows validation rules and selectors to access subject-level attributes efficiently, without needing to re-scan the directory structure or re-parse metadata for every individual file.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: This namespace enables context-aware validation at the subject level. It allows rules to enforce consistency across all files belonging to a single subject, such as verifying that required sessions are present or that subject-level metadata aligns with the files found in the directory. It improves validation efficiency and accuracy by scoping subject-specific checks appropriately, ensuring that rules do not incorrectly apply across different subjects.
example_scenarios: While validating `sub-01/ses-01/func/sub-01_ses-01_task-rest_bold.nii.gz`, the validator uses the `subject` namespace to check if `ses-01` is listed in the subject's session collection, ensuring the file's session entity matches the expected structure for that subject.
A custom validation rule queries `subject.participant_id` (derived from `participants.tsv`) to apply specific metadata checks only to subjects belonging to a particular cohort or demographic group.

When processing multiple files in `sub-02/anat/`, the `subject` namespace remains constant, allowing cross-file rules to verify that all expected anatomical modalities for `sub-02` are present before flagging missing files.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Not applicable. This record describes a conceptual component of the BIDS validation context, not a validation error or warning requiring resolution.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `subject` namespace is constructed once per subject directory, unlike the `dataset` namespace which remains constant across the entire dataset, or file-level namespaces (like `sidecar` or `entities`) which are updated for each individual file. It is primarily used by selectors and assertions within the BIDS schema to scope rules appropriately and is queried using object dot notation (e.g., `subject.sessions`).

title: Context Namespace: path
summary: The 'path' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'path' context namespace provides access to path information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The `path` context namespace provides the file path of the current BIDS file being inspected during validation, along with parsed components such as `entities`, `datatype`, `suffix`, `extension`, and `modality`. It is automatically populated by the BIDS Validator as it traverses the dataset.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When the BIDS Manager or Validator evaluates a file, the `path` namespace holds the file's location string and its decomposed BIDS filename parts. Validation rules reference this namespace to check if a file is in the correct directory, has the correct suffix, or matches expected associations.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate path information is fundamental to BIDS compliance, as the standard relies heavily on directory structure and filename conventions to organize and locate data. Validation rules use the `path` context to enforce these structural requirements.
example_scenarios: A validation rule checks if a `.nii.gz` file is located inside an `anat/` directory by inspecting `context.path` for the `/anat/` substring.
During validation of a T1-weighted image, the `path` context provides `datatype: "anat"`, `suffix: "T1w"`, and `extension: ".nii.gz"`, which rules use to verify correct naming.
A rule verifying that a sidecar JSON file is in the same directory as its corresponding NIfTI file uses the `path` context to compare directory locations.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This is an internal context namespace used by the validator. Users do not need to manually resolve or modify it. If validation fails related to paths, verify that the actual file's location and filename strictly follow BIDS naming conventions and directory structure requirements.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `path` context is part of the broader validation context object, which also includes `dataset`, `subject`, `sidecar`, and `associations` information. It is populated dynamically for each file as the validator iterates through the dataset.

summary: The 'size' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'size' context namespace provides access to size information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'size' context namespace provides the size of the current file being inspected during BIDS validation. It is a required component of the validation context and is automatically populated for every file processed by the validator.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When the BIDS Validator examines a dataset, it constructs a context object for each file. The 'size' namespace within this object contains the file's size (typically in bytes). This value is accessible to validation rules and selectors to enforce or check file-size-related constraints without requiring the validator to parse the file's internal structure.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: File size information allows validation rules to detect anomalies, such as unexpectedly large or small files, which might indicate corrupted data, incorrect compression, or missing content. It ensures the validator has access to basic file metadata efficiently.
example_scenarios: A validation rule compares the 'size' of a NIfTI file against the expected size calculated from its header dimensions and data type to detect potential corruption.
The validator flags a .nii.gz file that is unusually small, suggesting it might be empty, truncated, or incorrectly compressed.
A rule uses the 'size' namespace to verify that a sidecar JSON file is not excessively large, which could indicate malformed or duplicated metadata.

ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This is an informational namespace automatically provided by the validator. Users do not need to manually set or modify it. If validation rules fail based on file size, users should inspect the actual file for corruption, compression issues, or incorrect data types.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The 'size' namespace is defined as an integer in the BIDS Validator's context schema. It is part of the core context properties required for all file inspections, alongside 'path', 'dataset', 'sidecar', and 'associations'.

title: Context Namespace: entities
summary: The 'entities' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'entities' context namespace provides access to entities information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The entities context namespace provides a structured, programmatic representation of the key-value pairs extracted from a BIDS filename during validation. It maps directly to the hyphen-separated components (e.g., sub-01, ses-02, task-rest) that identify a file's subject, session, task, run, and other attributes.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager or the BIDS Validator inspects a file, it parses the file path and populates the entities namespace with these extracted components. This namespace is dynamically constructed for each file and allows validation rules or queries to access filename attributes using dot notation (e.g., entities.subject or entities.task). It serves as the bridge between the physical filename structure and the logical data attributes used in validation logic.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Entities are the foundation of BIDS file identification and organization. By exposing them in the validation context, the system can enforce naming conventions, verify that required entities are present, and ensure consistency across related files (such as matching run indices between imaging data and their sidecar metadata). Understanding this namespace helps users debug validation rules and comprehend how the validator interprets filenames.
example_scenarios: During validation of sub-01/ses-01/func/sub-01_ses-01_task-rest_run-01_bold.nii.gz, the entities namespace is populated with subject: 01, session: 01, task: rest, run: 01, datatype: func, suffix: bold, and extension: .nii.gz. A validation rule can then query entities.task to ensure all functional files for this subject use the same task name.
A user queries entities.subject to verify that a specific JSON sidecar file correctly corresponds to the anatomical scan it accompanies, ensuring that entity values match across associated files.

The validator uses the entities namespace to check that run indices are non-negative integers and properly formatted, as required by BIDS naming conventions for multiple acquisitions within the same session.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The entities namespace is automatically populated by the validator as it parses file paths and does not include metadata from sidecar JSON files, which are stored separately in the sidecar namespace. Entity values are typically strings, though some may be coerced to integers or floats depending on the specific entity definition. The order and presence of entities in filenames are governed by the BIDS specification's entity table and canonical ordering rules.

title: Context Namespace: datatype
summary: The 'datatype' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'datatype' context namespace provides access to datatype information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The `datatype` context namespace provides the data type directory name of the file currently being validated (e.g., `anat`, `func`, `dwi`, `eeg`). It is derived directly from the file's path within the BIDS dataset structure.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager or the BIDS Validator inspects a file, it extracts the `datatype` from the directory structure (e.g., `sub-01/anat/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz` yields `anat`). This value is used by validation rules to determine which schema definitions, metadata requirements, and naming conventions apply to the file.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The data type dictates the set of allowed entities, suffixes, and sidecar metadata fields for a file. Correctly identifying the datatype ensures that validation rules are applied accurately and that the dataset structure aligns with BIDS standards.
example_scenarios: A file located at `sub-01/func/sub-01_task-rest_bold.nii.gz` has a `datatype` context value of `func`, triggering validation rules specific to functional MRI data.

Physiological recordings (e.g., respiration, ECG) collected during an fMRI scan should be placed in the `func/` directory, not in a separate `ecg/` or `respiration/` directory, because the `datatype` context will correctly route them to functional data validation rules.
A file incorrectly placed in a root-level directory without a valid BIDS data type (e.g., `ecg/`) will fail validation because `ecg` is not a recognized BIDS datatype.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This is an informational context namespace, not an error or warning. Users do not need to resolve anything; the validator automatically extracts this value from the file path. Ensure files are placed in the correct BIDS-defined data type directories (e.g., `anat`, `func`, `dwi`, `meg`, `eeg`, `ieeg`, `beh`) to ensure proper validation.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: BIDS defines a specific set of data types. Files should not use custom directory names for data types unless they are explicitly supported (e.g., `phenotype` or `derivatives`). Physiological data should generally be grouped under the modality they accompany (like `func` or `dwi`) rather than creating new datatype directories.

title: Context Namespace: extension
summary: The 'extension' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'extension' context namespace provides access to extension information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'extension' context namespace is a built-in variable provided by the BIDS Validator during dataset inspection. It stores the file extension (e.g., '.nii.gz', '.json', '.tsv') of the current file being validated. This information is automatically extracted from the file path and made available to validation rules and custom checks.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When the BIDS Manager or Validator processes a file, it parses the filename and populates the 'context' object with various attributes. The 'context.extension' attribute specifically holds the suffix and extension of the file as it appears in the filename. This allows validation rules to conditionally apply checks based on file type without requiring hardcoded filename pattern matching.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Knowing the file extension is fundamental to BIDS validation because different file types have distinct structural requirements, metadata schemas, and associated rules. The validator uses this context to route files to the correct validation logic, verify that required associations (like sidecar JSON files) match expected extensions, and ensure that parsers are invoked for the correct file format.
example_scenarios: A validation rule checks if context.extension equals '.json' to ensure that a sidecar file contains valid JSON metadata before applying JSON-specific schema checks.
When validating a NIfTI image, the validator uses context.extension (e.g., '.nii.gz') to determine which NIfTI header parsing routine to invoke and which header fields to inspect.
A custom validator script iterates through a dataset and uses context.extension to group '.tsv' files separately from '.json' files for column-type validation.
common_causes: Automatically populated by the validator's internal path parser during file inspection
Used internally to route validation logic to the correct file-type handlers and schema validators
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: No user action is required to set or modify this value, as it is automatically derived from the filename. If validation rules fail due to extension-related issues, verify that the file extension in the filename matches the actual file format and adheres to BIDS naming conventions (e.g., using '.nii.gz' instead of '.nii' or '.gz').
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The 'context' object aggregates multiple namespaces including dataset, path, size, entities, datatype, suffix, extension, subject, sidecar, and associations. The extension field specifically captures the full extension string as it appears in the filename, which may include compound extensions like '.nii.gz'. This is part of the validator's buildFileContext routine and is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

title: Context Namespace: modality
summary: The 'modality' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'modality' context namespace provides access to modality information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'modality' context namespace is an inferred string property available during BIDS validation for the current file being inspected. It represents the category of brain data recorded by the file (e.g., 'mri', 'eeg', 'meg', 'ieeg', 'beh'). It is derived from the file's suffix and data type, and is accessible within the validation context for rules and selectors.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager inspects a file, the 'modality' namespace indicates the broad category of data recorded. This is an inferred property distinct from the BIDS 'data type', which refers to the directory name (e.g., anat, func, eeg). For MRI data, different pulse sequences (like T1w, bold, dwi) are considered distinct modalities. For passive recordings (EEG, MEG, iEEG), the recording technique itself defines the modality. The modality may overlap with the data type but should not be confused with it.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Distinguishing between modality and data type is essential for correctly organizing dataset directories and writing accurate validation rules. The validator uses the inferred modality to apply modality-specific checks and ensure files conform to BIDS naming and structural conventions.
example_scenarios: A structural MRI file located at sub-01/anat/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz has a data type of 'anat' but an inferred modality of 'mri'.
An EEG recording file at sub-01/eeg/sub-01_task-rest_eeg.vhdr has both a data type and a modality of 'eeg'.
A behavioral events file at sub-01/beh/sub-01_task-rest_events.tsv has a data type of 'beh' and a modality of 'beh'.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Not applicable. This is a conceptual namespace used during validation, not an error or warning.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: In the BIDS Validator context structure, 'modality' is nested under the 'path' object as an inferred property. It is automatically calculated by the validator based on the file's suffix and directory location, and is available to all rules evaluating that file.

title: Context Namespace: sidecar
summary: The 'sidecar' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'sidecar' context namespace provides access to sidecar information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The `sidecar` context namespace provides programmatic access to the metadata of the current file being validated. It is populated by loading the associated sidecar JSON file and applying the BIDS metadata inheritance principle, merging metadata from parent directories and dataset-level files.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When the BIDS Validator inspects a file, it automatically constructs the `sidecar` namespace with the file's metadata. Users and schema validation rules can query this namespace using dot notation (e.g., `sidecar.RepetitionTime`) to access specific metadata fields. This namespace is available for all files in the dataset and is particularly useful for cross-referencing metadata with file properties or other sidecar fields during validation.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: It enables sophisticated validation rules that check for consistency between metadata and file properties (e.g., ensuring metadata matches NIfTI headers or TSV columns). It ensures that metadata is correctly inherited and accessible for rule evaluation, helping users catch inconsistencies or missing information early.
example_scenarios: A validation rule checks if the `RepetitionTime` in the sidecar matches the `pixdim[4]` value in the NIfTI header: `sidecar.RepetitionTime == nifti_header.pixdim[4]`.
A rule verifies that the `Units` field exists in the sidecar and equals `"mm"`: `"Units" in sidecar && sidecar.Units == "mm"`.
When validating a field map, a rule might check that `EchoTime` is less than a certain threshold: `sidecar.EchoTime < 0.5`.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `sidecar` namespace is automatically constructed for each file during validation. It applies the BIDS metadata inheritance principle, meaning metadata from parent directories or `dataset_description.json` is merged into the current file's sidecar. It is available for all files in the dataset, not just imaging files, though it is most commonly used with imaging and TSV sidecars.

title: Context Namespace: associations
summary: The 'associations' namespace is available during validation for the current file being inspected.
retrieval_text: The 'associations' context namespace provides access to associations information during BIDS validation. This namespace is available when visiting all files in a dataset or subject.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'associations' context namespace is a runtime container used by the BIDS Validator to store information about files that are linked to the currently inspected file. It is automatically populated during validation based on association selector rules defined in the BIDS schema. Each key in the namespace corresponds to a specific association type (e.g., 'aslcontext', 'sidecar'), and its value contains properties such as the file path, row counts, or other metadata needed for cross-file validation.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: For BIDS Manager users, this namespace is not a manual dataset structure but a dynamic, validator-generated object. When the validator processes a file, it automatically resolves and loads associated files (like sidecars, context files, or physio logs) and makes them available here. This allows validation rules to check relationships between files without requiring users to manually manage cross-file references.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Many BIDS validation rules depend on cross-file consistency, such as verifying that an ASL image has a corresponding context file with the correct number of rows, or that a functional image matches its sidecar metadata. The 'associations' namespace enables the validator to enforce these rules efficiently. Understanding it helps users troubleshoot validation errors that stem from missing, mismatched, or incorrectly formatted linked files.
example_scenarios: Validating an ASL time-series file (e.g., sub-01_task-rest_asl.nii.gz): The validator populates the 'associations' namespace with an 'aslcontext' entry pointing to the corresponding .tsv file. Validation rules then check if the context file exists and if its row count matches the number of volumes in the NIfTI file.

Validating a functional MRI image: The namespace may contain entries for its JSON sidecar, BVAL/BVEC files, or physio log files. The validator uses these to verify entity matching, file existence, and metadata consistency.

Validating a minimal structural T1-weighted image: In a simple dataset with no cross-file dependencies, the 'associations' namespace may appear as an empty object ({}) because no association selector rules apply to that specific file.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: This namespace is automatically generated by the BIDS Validator and does not require manual intervention. If validation fails due to association-related issues, users should verify that linked files follow standard BIDS naming conventions, share matching entities (e.g., subject, session, task), and contain the expected metadata or structure. The BIDS Manager can help identify missing or mismatched associated files by inspecting the validation context.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The 'associations' namespace is part of the BIDS Validator's internal validation context object, not a physical file or directory. Similar functionality is exposed in PyBIDS via the `BIDSFile.get_associations()` method. The exact contents depend on the BIDS schema version and the specific file being validated.

title: File Association: events
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'events' with extension '.tsv'.
retrieval_text: The 'events' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'events' association links a BIDS data file to its corresponding task events file (_events.tsv). This association is triggered for any file that is not a JSON sidecar (extension != '.json'). The _events.tsv file documents the timing and properties of experimental events, such as stimuli presentation or participant responses, and must contain at least onset and duration columns.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager processes a data file (e.g., .nii.gz, .eeg, .edf), it will search for a matching _events.tsv file. The search begins in the same directory and, because inherit is set to true, extends to parent directories following the BIDS Inheritance Principle. The condition extension != '.json' ensures that JSON sidecar files do not incorrectly trigger a search for an events file.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Task events files are essential for linking experimental design timing to acquired data. Proper association ensures that validation tools can verify the presence of required event documentation and that downstream analysis pipelines can correctly align event onsets with the corresponding data streams. It also supports multi-echo and multi-recording scenarios where a single events file applies to multiple data files.
example_scenarios: A functional MRI run file sub-01_task-nback_bold.nii.gz is associated with sub-01_task-nback_events.tsv located in the same func/ directory.
An EEG recording sub-01_task-rest_eeg.vhdr inherits an events.tsv file placed in the root dataset directory, applying to all sessions and participants.
A multi-echo BOLD file sub-01_task-cuedSGT_run-1_echo-1_bold.nii.gz shares the same sub-01_task-cuedSGT_run-1_events.tsv file with its echo-2 and echo-3 counterparts.
common_causes: Events file placed in a directory that is not the same or a parent of the data file.
Mismatched suffixes between the data file and the events file (e.g., different task names).
JSON sidecar files incorrectly triggering events association searches due to missing extension filters.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that the _events.tsv file shares the same suffix (e.g., task name) as the data file. Ensure the events file is located in the same directory as the data file or in a parent directory if it is intended to be shared. Confirm that the data file is not a JSON sidecar, as the association rule explicitly excludes JSON files.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: According to the BIDS specification, events.tsv files MUST include onset and duration columns. They may be accompanied by an events.json sidecar to define optional columns. The association supports various modalities including fMRI, EEG, MEG, iEEG, and others. For multi-echo acquisitions, a single events file applies to all echoes of a run.

title: File Association: aslcontext
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'aslcontext' with extension '.tsv'.
retrieval_text: The 'aslcontext' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: The `aslcontext` association defines the relationship between a 4D Arterial Spin Labeling (ASL) NIfTI file (`_asl.nii.gz`) and its accompanying context file (`_aslcontext.tsv`). The context file is a tab-separated values file containing a single `volume_type` column that identifies the physiological or processed nature of each volume in the ASL time series (e.g., `control`, `label`, `m0scan`, `deltam`, or `cbf`).
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager processes an `_asl.nii.gz` file, it applies this association rule to locate the corresponding `_aslcontext.tsv`. The rule supports the BIDS inheritance principle, allowing the context file to be defined at the session or subject level to apply to multiple runs. While the specification permits this inheritance, some older validator versions may incorrectly flag top-level context files as invalid, which is generally considered a validator limitation rather than a spec violation.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate volume type annotation is critical for ASL processing pipelines to correctly apply mathematical models and compute cerebral blood flow (CBF) maps. The context file also drives validation of the associated `_asl.json` sidecar, as certain metadata fields (e.g., `M0Type`, `ArterialSpinLabelingType`) are conditionally required or forbidden based on the volume types present in the context file.
example_scenarios: A participant undergoes two ASL runs with identical acquisition parameters. The `_aslcontext.tsv` is placed at the subject level. BIDS Manager inherits it for both runs, avoiding file duplication.
A scanner exports a pre-processed `deltam` timeseries instead of raw `control`/`label` volumes. The `_aslcontext.tsv` lists `deltam` for the first N volumes and `m0scan` for the last volume.

A user places `_aslcontext.tsv` at the dataset root to apply to all ASL data. An outdated BIDS Validator may return a 'Files with such naming scheme are not part of BIDS specification' error, despite the spec supporting inheritance.
common_causes: Missing `_aslcontext.tsv` file for an `_asl.nii.gz` file.
Mismatched or misspelled volume type labels in the TSV file.
Using an outdated BIDS Validator that does not fully support inheritance for this specific association.
Inconsistent metadata between `_aslcontext.tsv` and `_asl.json` (e.g., `M0Type` set to `Separate` but no `m0scan` volume in the context file).
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that every `_asl.nii.gz` file has a corresponding `_aslcontext.tsv` in the same directory or a parent directory. Ensure the `volume_type` column contains valid BIDS ASL volume types. Cross-check the context file with the `_asl.json` sidecar to ensure metadata fields align with the listed volume types. If using an older validator that incorrectly flags inherited context files, update the validator or place the file in the run directory.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `_aslcontext.tsv` file contains exactly one column named `volume_type`. The BIDS Validator's context model explicitly tracks this association, exposing properties like `path`, `n_rows`, and `volume_type` for programmatic validation. The association is strictly tied to the `asl` suffix and NIfTI extensions, as defined in the schema.

title: File Association: m0scan
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'm0scan' with extension '['.nii', '.nii.gz']'.
retrieval_text: The 'm0scan' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files are expected in the same directory level.

ai_enrichment.description: The `m0scan` association rule identifies when a BIDS dataset contains an Arterial Spin Labeling (ASL) time-series file (`_asl.nii[.gz]`) and checks for the presence of a corresponding M0 reference scan (`_m0scan.nii[.gz]`). The M0 scan provides the single-point reference image required to quantify perfusion values from ASL data.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When the validator encounters an `_asl.nii[.gz]` file, it applies this association to verify that the M0 reference data is available. The M0 scan may be stored as a separate file or embedded within the ASL time-series. If stored separately, the `_asl.json` sidecar must explicitly link the two files using the `IntendedFor` field, and the `M0Type` field must indicate that the M0 scan is external.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate quantification of cerebral blood flow (CBF) from ASL data requires the M0 reference scan. Without it, or if it is incorrectly linked, downstream processing pipelines will fail or produce inaccurate perfusion maps. The association ensures data integrity and proper metadata linkage before analysis.
example_scenarios: A user acquires a separate M0 scan and saves it as `sub-01_m0scan.nii.gz`. The validator uses this association to confirm the file exists alongside `sub-01_asl.nii.gz` and checks that `_asl.json` contains the correct `IntendedFor` and `M0Type` metadata.

A scanner exports the M0 scan as the first volume of the 4D ASL file. In this case, no separate `_m0scan.nii[.gz]` file is created. The association rule's check is satisfied because the M0 data is embedded, and the `_asl.json` file will specify `M0Type: "embedded"`.

A user forgets to add the `IntendedFor` field to `_asl.json` when providing a separate M0 scan. The association highlights the missing link, prompting the user to add the relative path to the ASL file in the JSON sidecar.
common_causes: Triggers automatically when an `_asl.nii[.gz]` file is detected in the dataset.
Relevant for datasets storing the M0 reference scan separately from the ASL time-series, or when verifying that the necessary reference data is correctly paired with the ASL file.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that the `_asl.json` sidecar file contains the `M0Type` field set to either `"embedded"` or `"external"`. If `"external"`, ensure the `IntendedFor` field correctly points to the `_asl.nii[.gz]` file using a relative path. If the M0 scan is embedded, no separate `_m0scan.nii[.gz]` file is needed.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `m0scan` suffix is specific to Arterial Spin Labeling (ASL) data. While the association rule looks for a separate file, BIDS allows the M0 scan to be embedded in the ASL time-series to reduce storage and simplify file management. The `IntendedFor` field is required in `_asl.json` when the M0 scan is stored externally.

title: File Association: magnitude
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'magnitude' with extension '['.nii', '.nii.gz']'.
retrieval_text: The 'magnitude' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files are expected in the same directory level.

ai_enrichment.description: This association rule defines the expected pairing between a BIDS fieldmap image and its corresponding magnitude reference image. When a file with the suffix fieldmap and a NIfTI extension is found, the system searches for a companion file with the suffix magnitude in the same directory, sharing identical entities.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: In BIDS, a fieldmap image contains precomputed magnetic field inhomogeneity data (e.g., in Hz or rad/s), often generated directly by the scanner software. This data is typically paired with a magnitude image, which serves as a structural reference for coregistration during distortion correction. This association rule ensures that BIDS tools and validators can automatically locate the reference image needed to align the fieldmap correction to the subject's anatomy.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Distortion correction pipelines rely on the magnitude image to coregister the fieldmap to functional or anatomical data. If the association fails to find a matching magnitude file, downstream processing may report a missing associated file or lack the necessary reference for accurate spatial alignment.
example_scenarios: A dataset contains sub-01_acq-2ch_fieldmap.nii.gz and sub-01_acq-2ch_magnitude.nii.gz. The association correctly links them, allowing tools to use the magnitude image for coregistration.

A user provides sub-01_acq-2ch_fieldmap.nii.gz but omits the magnitude file. The validator or BIDS layout tools may report a missing associated file, and processing tools might lack the necessary reference for alignment.

A user incorrectly names the reference image as sub-01_acq-2ch_magnitude1.nii.gz (which is reserved for dual-echo phase difference schemes) instead of sub-01_acq-2ch_magnitude.nii.gz, causing the association rule to fail to match the files.
common_causes: Missing magnitude reference file in the fmap/ directory.
Incorrect suffix usage (e.g., magnitude1 or magnitude2 instead of magnitude).
Entity mismatch between the fieldmap and magnitude filenames.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that a magnitude NIfTI file exists in the same fmap/ directory as the fieldmap file. Ensure the filenames share identical entities (e.g., acq-, run-) and that the suffix is exactly magnitude. If the dataset uses a dual-echo gradient echo sequence, magnitude1/magnitude2 may be appropriate instead, but they follow a different association scheme.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The magnitude suffix in this context specifically refers to the single reference image paired with a precomputed fieldmap suffix. It is distinct from magnitude1 and magnitude2, which are used in two-phase image schemes where phase difference maps are calculated from separate phase and magnitude pairs.

title: File Association: magnitude1
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'magnitude1' with extension '['.nii', '.nii.gz']'.
retrieval_text: The 'magnitude1' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files are expected in the same directory level.

ai_enrichment.description: The `magnitude1` association defines the expected relationship between magnitude images and phase images in MRI fieldmap datasets. When a file with a suffix matching `phase1` or `phasediff` (and NIfTI extensions) is encountered, BIDS Manager searches for a corresponding `magnitude1` file to establish the pairing required for fieldmap-based distortion correction.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: This association rule instructs BIDS Manager how to automatically link magnitude and phase files. It ensures that when processing or validating a phase image, the system can locate its paired magnitude reference based on shared entities (subject, session, acquisition, run, chunk) and identical directory placement. The rule does not enforce a requirement but guides the software in resolving file relationships.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate pairing of magnitude and phase images is essential for calculating fieldmaps and correcting geometric distortions in functional and diffusion MRI data. Misassociation or missing magnitude files can lead to failed distortion correction, incorrect fieldmap generation, or downstream pipeline errors. Proper association also helps validators and layout tools correctly interpret the dataset structure.
example_scenarios: A user has `sub-01_acq-SE_fieldmap_phase1.nii.gz` and `sub-01_acq-SE_fieldmap_magnitude1.nii.gz`. The association rule automatically links them because they share identical entities and reside in the same `fmap/` directory.

If a user provides `sub-01_phasediff.nii.gz` but lacks a corresponding `sub-01_magnitude1.nii.gz`, the association will fail to resolve, which may trigger a validation warning about missing associated files or cause downstream tools to skip distortion correction.

In dual-echo acquisitions, `phase1` is typically paired with `magnitude1`, while `phase2` pairs with `magnitude2`. This specific association targets `phase1` and `phasediff` suffixes to find the primary magnitude reference.
common_causes: Missing magnitude file in the expected `fmap/` directory.
Mismatched entities (e.g., different `acq-`, `run-`, or `chunk-` labels) between the phase and magnitude files.
Incorrect suffix naming (e.g., using `phase` instead of `phase1` or `phasediff`).
Files placed in different directory levels, violating the same-directory expectation.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that the phase file and its associated magnitude file share identical entity values (excluding suffix and extension). Ensure both files are located in the same `fmap/` subdirectory. Confirm that the magnitude file uses the correct `magnitude1` suffix and a supported NIfTI extension (`.nii` or `.nii.gz`). If the dataset uses a dual-echo configuration with `phase2`, check for a separate association rule targeting `phase2` to link with `magnitude2`.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: According to the BIDS specification, fieldmap datasets may use single-echo (`phasediff` + `magnitude1`/`magnitude2`) or dual-echo (`phase1`/`phase2` + `magnitude1`/`magnitude2`) configurations. The selector `phase(diff|1)$` explicitly matches `phase1` and `phasediff`, but not `phase2`. This is consistent with how single-echo and dual-echo setups are often handled, though dual-echo pipelines may require additional association definitions for the second echo. The association itself is a structural guideline used by layout tools and validators to infer relationships, not a strict BIDS requirement.

title: File Association: bval
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'unknown' with extension '.bval'.
retrieval_text: The 'bval' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'bval' association links a NIfTI image file (with suffix 'dwi' or 'epi') to a corresponding '.bval' metadata file. This file contains space-delimited b-values (in s/mm²) that define the diffusion weighting strength for each volume in the associated NIfTI image. The association supports inheritance, allowing the '.bval' file to be placed in the same directory or any parent directory.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager processes a dataset, it will automatically search for a '.bval' file that matches the NIfTI file's suffix and entities. If the file is not found locally, it will traverse up the directory tree to find an applicable inherited file, provided it meets BIDS inheritance rules (same suffix, no extra entities, and at the same or higher directory level). The system expects the '.bval' file to contain exactly one b-value per volume in the NIfTI image.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate association of '.bval' files is essential for diffusion MRI preprocessing and analysis pipelines. These values dictate how diffusion gradients are applied to each volume. Validation tools explicitly check that the number of b-values in the file matches the number of volumes in the NIfTI image; a mismatch triggers a 'VOLUME_COUNT_MISMATCH' error. Incorrect or missing associations can cause preprocessing failures or biologically inaccurate results.
example_scenarios: A researcher places 'sub-01_dwi.nii.gz' and 'sub-01_dwi.bval' in the 'dwi/' folder. The association matches directly based on filename and suffix.

To avoid repetition, a researcher places 'dwi/sub-01_dwi.bval' in the dataset root. Due to the 'inherit: true' setting, BIDS Manager correctly associates it with 'dwi/sub-01_dwi.nii.gz' because it shares the suffix and lacks extra entities.

A validation error occurs when 'sub-01_dwi.nii.gz' contains 12 volumes, but the associated 'sub-01_dwi.bval' file only lists 10 space-delimited values. The validator flags this as a volume count mismatch.
common_causes: Missing '.bval' file in the expected directory or parent directories.
Filename entities in the '.bval' file do not match the NIfTI file, breaking the association or inheritance lookup.
Mismatch between the number of volumes in the NIfTI image and the number of b-values listed in the file.
Incorrect file format (e.g., using commas instead of spaces, or missing the FSL space-delimited structure).
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that the '.bval' filename exactly matches the NIfTI filename, differing only by the extension. Ensure the file contains space-delimited b-values corresponding to each volume, with '0' indicating non-diffusion-weighted (b0) volumes. If using inheritance, confirm the file is placed at a directory level that satisfies BIDS rules (same or higher level, matching suffix, no extra entities). Check that the volume count in the NIfTI header matches the number of values in the '.bval' file.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The '.bval' file is part of the FSL format for diffusion data and is typically paired with a '.bvec' file containing gradient directions. BIDS allows these files to be stored at any directory level, but the validator enforces that only the applicable file lowest in the hierarchy is used. The association also applies to 'epi' suffixes because Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) is the standard readout sequence for diffusion-weighted scans in BIDS.

title: File Association: bvec
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'unknown' with extension '.bvec'.
retrieval_text: The 'bvec' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: The `bvec` association defines how BIDS Manager links diffusion-weighted imaging (dwi) or echo-planar imaging (epi) NIfTI files to their corresponding gradient direction vector files. This association is governed by BIDS' Inheritance Principle, which dictates that the validator searches for the applicable `.bvec` file starting from the data file's directory and moving upward to the dataset root. The file located lowest in the filesystem hierarchy that matches the suffix and entity constraints is selected.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When working with BIDS Manager, this means that `bvec` files are not strictly required to sit in the same folder as their corresponding NIfTI images. Instead, they can be placed in parent directories and will automatically apply to matching data files in subdirectories. However, you must ensure that only one applicable `bvec` file exists at any given directory level for a specific suffix and entity combination. The validator will prioritize the `bvec` file closest to the data file.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate association of `bvec` files is essential for downstream diffusion MRI processing pipelines, as gradient direction information is required for image reconstruction, motion correction, and tractography. Misunderstanding the inheritance rules can lead to validators flagging conflicts or processing software reading incorrect gradient directions, resulting in artifacts or failed analyses.
example_scenarios: A researcher places `sub-01_dwi.bvec` in the `sub-01/dwi/` directory. This file is automatically associated with all `sub-01_dwi_*.nii.gz` files in that folder and any subdirectories, unless overridden by a more specific file.

A dataset contains multiple acquisitions with different gradient schemes. The researcher places a general `sub-01_dwi.bvec` in `sub-01/dwi/` and a specific `sub-01_dwi_acq-highres.bvec` in `sub-01/dwi/sub-01_acq-highres/`. The validator correctly associates the specific file with the high-resolution data and the general file with the rest.

A user accidentally copies `sub-01_dwi.bvec` into both `sub-01/dwi/` and `sub-01/dwi/sub-01_acq-test/`. If both files share the same suffix and entity subset relative to a target data file, the validator will flag a conflict because multiple applicable files exist at the same directory level.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify the directory structure to ensure that for any given data file, there is only one applicable `bvec` file at the lowest possible directory level. If you encounter association conflicts, check for duplicate `bvec` files at the same hierarchy level or ensure that entity names in the `bvec` filename do not exceed those in the data filename. Adjust file placement to align with the intended inheritance scope.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS specification and validator documentation emphasize that for simple metadata files like `bvec`, there is no concept of 'unsetting' or overriding specific values; the entire file is replaced by the lower-level file. The validator uses a 'walk back' algorithm to resolve associations, strictly following the rule that the applicable file must be at the same or higher directory level, share the same suffix, and contain no entities absent from the data filename.

title: File Association: channels
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'channels' with extension '.tsv'.
retrieval_text: The 'channels' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'channels' association links a physiological or motion data file to a corresponding tabular metadata file named with the suffix '_channels.tsv'. This metadata file describes the properties of each recording channel, such as its type, units, sampling frequency, hardware details, and groupings. The association follows BIDS inheritance rules, allowing the metadata file to be placed at the same directory level as the data file or in a higher-level directory to apply to multiple files.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager processes a data file with a suffix like 'eeg', 'ieeg', 'meg', 'emg', 'nirs', 'motion', or 'optodes', it automatically searches for a matching '_channels.tsv' file. Because inheritance is enabled, the manager will first look in the data file's directory, then traverse upward through parent directories to find the applicable metadata. The associated file must share the exact suffix of the data file and must not contain any entities that are absent from the data filename.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Channel metadata is critical for correctly interpreting raw recording data. It allows BIDS-compliant software and validation tools to understand channel configurations, sampling rates, and hardware specifications without relying on proprietary binary headers. Proper association ensures that analysis pipelines can automatically load, verify, and apply this metadata, preventing misinterpretation of signals or validation errors.
example_scenarios: A participant has a single 'sub-01_channels.tsv' file in the 'sub-01/eeg/' directory. BIDS Manager associates it with all EEG files in that folder due to the inheritance rule, avoiding the need to duplicate the file for each run.
A dataset contains 'sub-01_task-rest_channels.tsv' in the 'sub-01/eeg/' folder. This run-specific file overrides any participant-level 'sub-01_channels.tsv' exclusively for the resting-state task.

A user places 'sub-01_channels.tsv' in the dataset root directory. BIDS Manager still successfully associates it with 'sub-01/eeg/sub-01_eeg.vhdr' because it shares the 'eeg' suffix and resides at a higher directory level.
common_causes: Data files possess suffixes such as 'eeg', 'ieeg', 'meg', 'emg', 'nirs', 'motion', or 'optodes'.
A tabular file with the '_channels' suffix and '.tsv' extension exists in the same or a parent directory.
The metadata filename shares the exact suffix with the data file and contains no additional entities.
The metadata file is located at the same or a higher level in the filesystem hierarchy than the data file.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: To ensure proper association, verify that the '_channels.tsv' filename matches the data file's suffix (e.g., 'sub-01_eeg_channels.tsv' or 'sub-01_channels.tsv'). Place the file in the same directory as the data, or in a parent directory if it applies to multiple runs. Ensure the file extension is strictly '.tsv' and not '.json'. If validation fails, check that the metadata file does not contain entities absent from the data filename and that no other applicable metadata file exists at the same directory level.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The 'channels.tsv' file is highly recommended for iEEG and other modalities to facilitate browsing and searching channel properties like sampling frequency or electrode material. It should not be confused with 'electrodes.tsv', which stores spatial coordinates and should be kept separate. According to BIDS common principles, metadata files are loaded from the top of the directory hierarchy downwards, and values from higher levels are inherited unless overridden by a file at a lower level.

title: File Association: coordsystem
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'coordsystem' with extension '.json'.
retrieval_text: The 'coordsystem' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: The `coordsystem` association rule identifies when a BIDS dataset requires a `_coordsystem.json` sidecar file to define the coordinate system and units for electrode, optode, or sensor positions. This association is triggered for neurophysiological recording files (e.g., `.eeg`, `.ieeg`, `.meg`, `.nirs`) and descriptor files (e.g., `_electrodes.tsv`, `_optodes.tsv`) across modalities like EEG, iEEG, MEG, NIRS, EMG, and motion tracking.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager encounters a file with a suffix matching the selector rules, it automatically searches for an associated `_coordsystem.json` file. Following BIDS inheritance principles, the validator will look in the same directory first, then traverse up the directory tree to find the appropriate coordinate system definition. This mechanism ensures that coordinate system metadata is not duplicated across multiple task or run files, and that spatial coordinates in descriptor files are correctly interpreted.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: The `_coordsystem.json` file is mandatory if `_electrodes.tsv` or `_optodes.tsv` files are provided, as it specifies the coordinate system (e.g., `ACPC`, `RAS`, `NIRSCoordinateSystem`) and units (e.g., `mm`, `cm`) used for the spatial coordinates. Proper association ensures that downstream processing tools can correctly interpret electrode/optode locations, align them with anatomical scans, and validate dataset structure without redundant metadata.
example_scenarios: A user creates `sub-01_electrodes.tsv` to define electrode locations but forgets to create `sub-01_coordsystem.json`. The validator will flag a missing required coordinate system definition because the association rule cannot resolve a target file.

A dataset contains multiple task recordings (`task-rest_eeg.edf`, `task-nback_eeg.edf`) that share the same electrode layout. Instead of duplicating `sub-01_coordsystem.json` in every task folder, the user places it in the `sub-01/` directory, and BIDS inheritance correctly associates it with all task files.

Optodes are physically moved between two recording sessions. The specification recommends creating separate session folders (`ses-01/`, `ses-02/`) with distinct `_optodes.tsv` and `_coordsystem.json` files rather than duplicating the coordinate system across tasks within the same session.
common_causes: Missing `_coordsystem.json` when `_electrodes.tsv` or `_optodes.tsv` is present in the dataset.
Incorrectly duplicating `_coordsystem.json` files across multiple task directories instead of relying on BIDS inheritance.
Placing the coordinate system file in a directory that does not follow the inheritance path (e.g., putting it in a task folder when it should be in the subject or session folder).
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Ensure that a `_coordsystem.json` file exists in the same directory as the associated electrode/optode or recording file, or in a parent directory to leverage BIDS inheritance. Verify that the coordinate system and units specified in the JSON match the values used in the corresponding `.tsv` descriptor files. If multiple sessions involve different electrode/optode placements, organize them into separate session directories rather than duplicating metadata across tasks.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The association rule covers a wide range of suffixes including `motion` and `electrodes`, reflecting BIDS extensions for motion tracking and general electrode descriptions. The official specification emphasizes that `_coordsystem.json` files SHOULD NOT be duplicated for each data file and that the inheritance principle MUST be used. If electrodes or optodes are repositioned, using multiple sessions is the recommended approach.

title: File Association: electrodes
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'electrodes' with extension '.tsv'.
retrieval_text: The 'electrodes' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: Defines the BIDS association rule for `_electrodes.tsv` files, which store the physical locations and properties of recording electrodes. The rule triggers for EEG, EMG, iEEG, and MEG data files and requires the `space` entity to specify the coordinate system.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When BIDS Manager encounters an EEG, EMG, iEEG, or MEG data file, it will look for a corresponding `_electrodes.tsv` file. Because inheritance is enabled, the validator will search up the directory tree if the file is not in the same folder. The presence of the `space` entity indicates that the electrode coordinates are defined in a specific anatomical or stereotaxic coordinate system, which must be documented in a matching `_coordsystem.json` file.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Properly associating electrode files ensures that spatial metadata is correctly linked to the recorded signals. BIDS mandates the use of inheritance to avoid duplicating electrode position files across multiple runs or sessions. Additionally, the `space` entity links the electrode positions to a defined coordinate system, which is critical for neuroimaging analysis and interoperability.
example_scenarios: An EEG dataset with 5 runs of a task. Instead of creating five separate `_electrodes.tsv` files, a single file is placed in the `sub-01/eeg/` directory. BIDS Manager inherits it for all run-specific data files.

An iEEG dataset where electrodes are coregistered to a standard template. The file is named `sub-01_ses-01_space-MNI152Lin_electrodes.tsv`, and the `space-MNI152Lin` entity triggers the association rule.
A MEG dataset with electrodes localized in a subject-specific anatom space. The file uses `space-individual` and is paired with a corresponding `sub-01_space-individual_coordsystem.json`.
common_causes: Missing `_coordsystem.json` when `_electrodes.tsv` is present.
Duplicating `_electrodes.tsv` files for each run instead of using inheritance.
Mismatched or missing `space` entity labels between `_electrodes.tsv` and `_coordsystem.json`.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that the `_electrodes.tsv` file is placed at the appropriate directory level to allow inheritance, or move it to the data file's directory if it is run-specific. Ensure a corresponding `_coordsystem.json` file exists with a matching `space` label. Avoid creating multiple copies of the electrode file across runs.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The `electrodes.tsv` file describes the physical recording sites (electrodes), whereas `channels.tsv` describes the recorded signals (channels). While often used interchangeably in practice, BIDS distinguishes them. The `space` entity is specifically required when electrode positions are given in an anatomical or stereotaxic coordinate system.

title: File Association: physio
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'physio' with extension '.tsv.gz'.
retrieval_text: The 'physio' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files are expected in the same directory level.

ai_enrichment.description: The 'physio' association targets files containing physiological and other continuous recordings, such as cardiac, respiratory, motion parameters, or eyetracking data. These files are expected to use the '_physio' suffix and '.tsv.gz' extension, accompanied by a '.json' sidecar for metadata.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: In BIDS Manager, this association rule identifies physiological data files by matching any file that does not have a '.json' extension. It ensures that the system correctly recognizes continuous recordings and links them to their corresponding metadata sidecars. The selector 'extension != ".json"' explicitly excludes JSON sidecars from being treated as data files themselves, preventing false matches during file resolution.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly associating physiological files ensures that analysis pipelines can locate continuous recordings and their metadata. BIDS specifies that these TSV files do not include header lines; instead, column names and units are defined in the accompanying JSON sidecar. Proper association prevents validation errors, ensures compatibility with tools like PyBIDS (which may automatically link these files to imaging runs via IntendedFor/InformedBy), and maintains consistency across modalities like func, beh, anat, dwi, and eeg.
example_scenarios: A user has a file named 'sub-01_task-rest_physio.tsv.gz' containing respiratory data. The association rule matches this file because it lacks a '.json' extension, allowing BIDS Manager to recognize it as physiological data and look for 'sub-01_task-rest_physio.json'.

To distinguish between different signals recorded during the same task, a user names files 'sub-01_task-rest_recording-breathing_physio.tsv.gz' and 'sub-01_task-rest_recording-cardiac_physio.tsv.gz'. The association applies to both, as they match the selector and suffix requirements.

A shared physiological recording for a movie-watching task is placed in the root directory as 'task-movie_stim.tsv.gz'. The association helps identify this file across the dataset structure without requiring subject-specific prefixes.
common_causes: Files are missing the required '_physio' suffix or '.tsv.gz' extension.
The accompanying '.json' sidecar is missing, which is required to define column names since the TSV file is headerless.
A header row is incorrectly included in the TSV file, violating BIDS formatting rules for physiological data.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that physiological data files follow the naming convention '<matches>[_recording-<label>]_physio.tsv.gz'. Ensure a corresponding '<matches>[_recording-<label>]_physio.json' file exists in the same directory to specify sampling frequency, start time, and column definitions. Confirm that the TSV file does not contain a header row, as BIDS requires column names to be defined in the JSON sidecar. If multiple recordings exist for the same task, use the 'recording-' entity to differentiate them.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The 'recording-' entity can be used to differentiate multiple physiological recordings within the same task. Physiological files can be placed in various modality directories (e.g., func/, beh/, anat/, dwi/, eeg/, emg/, motion/, nirs/, perf/, pet/) or the dataset root if shared across subjects. PyBIDS automatically creates associations between these files and imaging runs using 'IntendedFor' or 'InformedBy' metadata. EMG data is also supported under this rule in BIDS v1.11.1+.

title: File Association: coordsystems
summary: Defines when to search for an associated file matching 'coordsystem' with extension '.json'.
retrieval_text: The 'coordsystems' association applies when file conditions match the selector rules. Associated files may be inherited from shallower directory levels.

ai_enrichment.description: This association rule defines how BIDS Manager automatically links EMG recording data (_emg.tsv) and electrode location files (_electrodes.tsv) to their corresponding coordinate system metadata files (_coordsystem.json). It specifies that the manager should search for a JSON file with the coordsystem suffix and a space entity, and it allows the search to inherit from parent directories according to BIDS metadata inheritance principles.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: When processing EMG or electrode files, BIDS Manager uses this rule to locate the _coordsystem.json file that describes the spatial reference frame for the data. Because inherit is set to true, the manager will look in the file's own directory first, then traverse upwards to parent directories until it finds a matching file. This aligns with the BIDS specification's requirement to use inheritance rather than duplicating coordinate system definitions across multiple tasks or runs.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Correctly associating electrode coordinates with their coordinate system definitions is essential for spatial analysis, source localization, and interoperability with other neuroimaging tools. Following the inheritance principle prevents redundant files, reduces maintenance overhead, and ensures that metadata resolution follows a predictable, standardized hierarchy.
example_scenarios: A subject has a single electrode cap setup used across multiple EMG tasks. Instead of creating a separate _coordsystem.json for each task file, the researcher places one _sub-01_coordsystem.json at the session level. BIDS Manager inherits this file for all task-specific _emg.tsv files.

An _electrodes.tsv file lists a CoordinateSystem column value of 'ACPC'. The associated _coordsystem.json file, located in the same directory or a parent directory, defines the ACPC coordinate system and its properties.

A user places _coordsystem.json files in both the subject directory and the task directory. BIDS Manager resolves this by applying the inheritance principle, using the file at the deeper (task) level to override or supplement the one at the shallower (subject) level, while ensuring no more than one applicable file exists at each directory level.
common_causes: Missing _coordsystem.json file in the expected directory hierarchy.
Placing multiple applicable _coordsystem.json files at the same directory level, violating the one file per level rule.
Duplicating _coordsystem.json across multiple task directories instead of relying on inheritance.
Mismatched or missing space entity in the coordinate system filename.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that a _coordsystem.json file exists at the same directory level as the EMG or electrode file, or in a parent directory. Ensure the filename includes the space entity if required by your data. Avoid creating duplicate coordinate system files for each task; instead, place a single file at the highest appropriate level and rely on BIDS inheritance. If overriding is necessary, place the new file in a deeper directory level.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS EEG/EMG extension explicitly recommends against duplicating _coordsystem.json files across tasks. The general BIDS inheritance principle applies: metadata is loaded from the top of the hierarchy downwards, with deeper files overriding shallower ones. There is no concept of unsetting a key-value pair once inherited.
