issue.message:
The fields 'VolumeTiming' and 'RepetitionTime' for this file are mutually exclusive.
Choose 'RepetitionTime' when the same repetition time is used for all volumes,
or 'VolumeTiming' when variable times are used.

ai_enrichment.description: This validation check enforces that the BIDS sidecar JSON for a functional or ASL NIfTI file contains either the 'RepetitionTime' field or the 'VolumeTiming' field, but never both. These two metadata fields describe the timing between image volumes and are mutually exclusive in the BIDS specification.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: The BIDS Validator has detected that both 'RepetitionTime' and 'VolumeTiming' are present in the JSON sidecar accompanying a '.nii' or '.nii.gz' file with a 'bold' or 'asl' suffix. To pass validation, you must remove one of these fields so that only the appropriate timing descriptor remains.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Both fields provide timing information for the acquired volumes. Specifying both creates ambiguity for downstream processing pipelines (e.g., slice timing correction, motion correction, or physiological noise regression), which expect a single, unambiguous definition of the scan timing structure. Resolving this conflict ensures that software tools can correctly interpret the temporal properties of your data.
example_scenarios: A researcher manually edits a sidecar JSON to add 'VolumeTiming' for a variable-TR acquisition but forgets to delete the existing 'RepetitionTime' field, triggering the error.
A dataset is converted from a non-BIDS format using a script that exports all available timing metadata into the same JSON file, resulting in both fields being written.
A user copies a sidecar JSON template from another dataset that uses constant TR, and pastes it into a new dataset that uses variable volume timing without cleaning up the template fields.
common_causes: Manual editing errors where a new timing field is added without removing the old one.
Automated conversion scripts that dump all available metadata without filtering for BIDS mutual exclusivity rules.
Copy-pasting JSON sidecars between datasets with different acquisition protocols.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the JSON sidecar file associated with the failing NIfTI file. Identify whether your acquisition used a constant repetition time or variable timing per volume. If the repetition time is constant, keep the 'RepetitionTime' field and delete 'VolumeTiming'. If the timing varies per volume, keep the 'VolumeTiming' array and delete 'RepetitionTime'. Save the file and re-run the validator.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: RepetitionTime is a single numeric value (in seconds) representing the time between the start of consecutive volumes. VolumeTiming is an array of numeric values (in seconds) representing the acquisition time of each individual volume relative to the start of the scan. Choose the field that best matches your scanner's acquisition protocol.

title: Validation Check: RepetitionTimeFrameAcquisitionDurationMutex

issue.message:
The fields 'RepetitionTime' and 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' for this file are mutually exclusive.
To specify acquisition duration, use 'SliceTiming' or 'DelayTime'

ai_enrichment.description: This validation check enforces the BIDS rule that the 'RepetitionTime' and 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' fields are mutually exclusive in functional imaging sidecar JSON files (e.g., for bold and asl suffixes). If 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' is present, 'RepetitionTime' must be omitted.

BIDS requires you to specify only one of these timing parameters. 'RepetitionTime' defines the interval between the start of consecutive volumes, while 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' defines the time taken to acquire a single volume. You must remove 'RepetitionTime' from the JSON to resolve this error.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate timing metadata is essential for correct temporal preprocessing, including slice timing correction, motion correction, and physiological noise regression. Providing conflicting or redundant timing fields can cause analysis software to miscalculate temporal offsets, leading to artifacts or failed preprocessing steps.
example_scenarios: A researcher manually edits a sidecar JSON to include 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' for a multiband sequence but forgets to delete the default 'RepetitionTime' field, triggering the validator error.
An automated metadata conversion script merges parameters from different scanner logs, inadvertently outputting both TR and FAD into the same BIDS sidecar.
A user attempts to document both the volume-to-volume interval and the volume acquisition duration, not realizing that BIDS treats these as alternative ways to describe acquisition timing.

Automated pipeline scripts that do not enforce BIDS mutual exclusivity rules when generating sidecars.
Copy-pasting metadata from non-BIDS formats without filtering out redundant timing fields.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the sidecar JSON file for the affected functional image and remove the 'RepetitionTime' field. Ensure that 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' accurately reflects your sequence parameters. If your sequence requires slice timing information, verify that the 'SliceTiming' field is also provided. For ASL data, consider using 'DelayTime' if applicable to describe post-labeling delays.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS specification enforces mutual exclusivity between these fields to prevent ambiguity in temporal calculations. 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' is particularly useful for sequences with multiband acceleration or variable acquisition times, where the time to acquire one volume differs from the interval between volumes. When 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' is used, downstream tools will rely on it instead of 'RepetitionTime' for timing-related operations.

title: Validation Check: VolumeTimingDelayTimeMutex

issue.message:
The fields 'VolumeTiming' and 'DelayTime' for this file are mutually exclusive.
To specify acquisition duration, use 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' or 'SliceTiming'.

ai_enrichment.description: This validation check enforces that the 'VolumeTiming' and 'DelayTime' fields in a BIDS sidecar JSON file are mutually exclusive. It triggers an error when both fields are present for functional imaging files (suffix 'bold' or 'asl') with NIfTI extensions, specifically when 'RepetitionTime' is not specified.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: BIDS requires a single, unambiguous method to describe volume acquisition timing. 'VolumeTiming' provides a list of relative acquisition times for each volume, while 'DelayTime' specifies a single delay value. The validator ensures users do not define both, as doing so creates conflicting timing information. The check is scoped to cases where 'RepetitionTime' is absent, which is common when 'VolumeTiming' is used to define acquisition schedules.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Ambiguous timing metadata can lead to incorrect slice timing correction, motion correction, or hemodynamic modeling in downstream analyses. Ensuring only one timing specification is present guarantees that processing pipelines interpret the acquisition schedule consistently.
example_scenarios: A researcher converts a legacy dataset that used 'DelayTime' and attempts to add 'VolumeTiming' to support interleaved slice acquisition, resulting in both fields being present in the JSON sidecar.
An automated conversion tool from a scanner-specific format incorrectly maps two different timing parameters to both 'DelayTime' and 'VolumeTiming'.
Manual editing of a sidecar JSON file accidentally leaves 'DelayTime' from a previous version while 'VolumeTiming' is added for a new analysis.
common_causes: Converting datasets from older BIDS versions or non-BIDS formats where multiple timing parameters were recorded.
Manual JSON editing errors where one field is not removed after adding the other.
Automated conversion scripts mapping scanner metadata to BIDS fields without checking for mutual exclusivity.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the sidecar JSON file for the affected functional image. Decide which timing parameter accurately reflects the acquisition protocol. If detailed relative timing per volume is needed, keep 'VolumeTiming' and remove 'DelayTime'. If only a single delay value is relevant, keep 'DelayTime' and remove 'VolumeTiming'. The error message also suggests using 'FrameAcquisitionDuration' or 'SliceTiming' if the intent is to specify acquisition duration rather than relative volume timing.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The presence of 'VolumeTiming' often implies that 'RepetitionTime' is not constant or is derived from the timing list itself, which is why the check specifically looks for cases where 'RepetitionTime' is null. 'DelayTime' is largely considered legacy in modern BIDS workflows when 'VolumeTiming' is available.

title: Validation Check: VolumeTimingMissingFrameAcquisitionDuration

checks:
"SliceTiming" in sidecar ||
"FrameAcquisitionDuration" in sidecar ||
"AcquisitionDuration" in sidecar

ai_enrichment.description: This validation check ensures that when the VolumeTiming field is present in a functional imaging sidecar (for bold or asl suffixes) without a corresponding RepetitionTime, at least one of SliceTiming, FrameAcquisitionDuration, or AcquisitionDuration is also provided.
ai_enrichment.interpretation: The BIDS Validator flags this as an error because VolumeTiming alone is insufficient to fully describe the temporal structure of the acquisition when RepetitionTime is absent. Providing FrameAcquisitionDuration (time to acquire one volume), SliceTiming (relative timing of slices), or AcquisitionDuration (total scan duration) gives downstream processing tools the necessary context to handle the data correctly.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Accurate temporal metadata is critical for fMRI preprocessing steps like slice-timing correction, motion correction, and physiological noise regression. Missing timing information can lead to incorrect realignment or misinterpretation of hemodynamic responses.
example_scenarios: A researcher exports fMRI data with non-standard TRs and provides VolumeTiming to list exact volume start times, but forgets to include FrameAcquisitionDuration to indicate how long each volume took to acquire.

An ASL dataset uses VolumeTiming to specify exact acquisition times for each volume, but lacks SliceTiming or FrameAcquisitionDuration, leaving the scanner unable to determine slice or volume acquisition duration.
A dataset migration tool automatically populates VolumeTiming from raw DICOM headers but omits RepetitionTime and the required duration fields, triggering the validator error.
common_causes: Using VolumeTiming to specify exact volume timings while omitting RepetitionTime, but failing to provide the necessary duration metadata (FrameAcquisitionDuration, SliceTiming, or AcquisitionDuration).
Automated conversion from proprietary formats that extracts volume timing but drops standard timing fields.
Incomplete sidecar JSON generation during data export.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Review the functional sidecar JSON file. If VolumeTiming is intentionally used to specify exact volume timings, add FrameAcquisitionDuration (to specify the duration of each volume), SliceTiming (if slice timing information is available), or AcquisitionDuration (total scan duration). Alternatively, if RepetitionTime is known, add it to the sidecar and consider removing VolumeTiming unless non-standard timing is required.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: VolumeTiming is an optional field in BIDS primarily intended for cases where the repetition time is not constant or when exact volume timings are known. When RepetitionTime is present, VolumeTiming is generally not needed unless there are specific timing irregularities.

Manual editing of sidecar files where deprecated fields were not removed during dataset restructuring.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Remove the 'AcquisitionDuration' field from the affected sidecar JSON files. If the duration of a single volume acquisition is known, replace it with 'FrameAcquisitionDuration'. title: Validation Check: SuspiciouslyLongBOLDDesign

ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Downstream fMRI analysis pipelines rely on accurate alignment between the timing of events and the acquired time series. Ensuring consistency between the NIfTI header and events.tsv is critical for valid hemodynamic response modeling.

A researcher accidentally copies the events.tsv file from a previous run that had 200 volumes (400 seconds) into a new dataset where the current run only has 100 volumes (200 seconds).
The onset times in the events.tsv file were exported from a stimulus presentation script that used milliseconds instead of seconds, causing all onsets to appear far beyond the scan duration.
common_causes: Mismatch between the number of volumes in the NIfTI file and the number of volumes expected by the events.tsv file.
Incorrect TR value in the NIfTI header or events.tsv metadata.
Copy-pasting events files between runs with different acquisition durations.
Unit conversion errors when generating the events.tsv file.
Scanner protocol changes that were not reflected in the events file.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify the number of volumes and TR in the BOLD NIfTI file's header. Cross-check these values against the events.tsv file to ensure all onset times fall within the range [0, TR * num_volumes). If the events file corresponds to a different run, replace it with the correct file. If the onset times were generated programmatically, check for unit conversion errors or incorrect offsets. Adjust the events.tsv or the NIfTI file to ensure consistency.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The raw content indicates this check produces a warning, while the scope metadata lists it as an error. In the official BIDS Validator, this is typically issued as a warning because it does not strictly violate the BIDS filename or structure rules, but it indicates a likely experimental design mismatch. The check relies on the NIfTI header values; if the header is missing or incorrect, the check may not run or may produce misleading results.

While not a BIDS compliance error, addressing it can improve downstream analysis quality and reproducibility.

ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Verify that the event onsets in the events file accurately reflect the timing relative to the BOLD scan start. If the design is suboptimal, consider redistributing events earlier in the run or extending the scan duration to allow for adequate baseline periods.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The threshold of 'half the scan duration' is an arbitrary heuristic chosen by the BIDS Validator developers to flag potentially inefficient designs. It is not a normative requirement in the BIDS specification. The check only applies to BOLD data with associated events files and relies on NIfTI header metadata to determine scan duration.

title: Validation Check: PhasePartUnits

ai_enrichment.description: This validation check verifies that the `Units` metadata field in the JSON sidecar for MRI phase images (files containing the `part-phase` entity) contains a valid value. If the corresponding JSON sidecar includes a `Units` key, the validator checks whether its value is exactly "rad" or "arbitrary". If the field is present but contains any other string (e.g., "degrees", "volts", or an empty value), the check fails and raises an error with code `PHASE_UNITS`. Note that this check only triggers if the `Units` field is explicitly present in the sidecar.
ai_enrichment.why_it_matters: Phase images are frequently used in quantitative MRI applications such as field mapping, susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI), and quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM). Downstream processing tools rely on accurate unit metadata to perform correct mathematical operations (e.g., converting phase to frequency shifts or calculating susceptibility values). Incorrect or non-standard units can lead to significant calculation errors or pipeline failures.
example_scenarios: A researcher exports phase data from a scanner that outputs values in degrees and sets "Units": "degrees" in the JSON sidecar without converting the NIfTI data to radians. The validator flags this because BIDS only accepts "rad" or "arbitrary".
A processing pipeline outputs phase data in raw digital counts, and the user incorrectly sets "Units": "counts" instead of the standardized "arbitrary".

A user copies a magnitude image sidecar to a phase image but forgets to update the metadata, resulting in a mismatched or incorrectly typed `Units` field that triggers validation issues when explicitly defined.
common_causes: Directly copying scanner-specific or third-party processing units (e.g., degrees, volts, ADC counts) into the BIDS sidecar.
Typos or case-sensitivity errors (e.g., using "Rad" or "RAD" instead of the required lowercase "rad").
Misunderstanding BIDS requirements for phase images, assuming units can be freely defined like in other modalities.
Automated conversion scripts that populate metadata without filtering for BIDS-compliant values.
ai_enrichment.resolution_guidance: Open the JSON sidecar associated with the failing `part-phase` file. Locate the `Units` field. If the data represents phase in radians, change the value to "rad". If the units are unknown, non-standard, or derived from arbitrary processing steps, change the value to "arbitrary". Ensure the value is strictly lowercase and matches one of the two allowed options exactly. If the `Units` field is not needed and was added by mistake, it can be removed, though keeping it as "rad" or "arbitrary" is recommended for clarity.
ai_enrichment.additional_notes: The BIDS specification treats magnitude (`part-mag`) and phase (`part-phase`) images differently regarding metadata requirements. While magnitude images often do not require a `Units` field, phase images have stricter conventions due to their role in quantitative analysis. Always ensure that the numerical values in the NIfTI file actually correspond to the declared units; changing the metadata without converting the underlying data will produce physically incorrect results.
